findings.title: The unsubscribe action changes preferences through a CSRF-able GET request
findings.body: This GET endpoint directly changes and saves the current user's notification preference, while it is explicitly allowed outside the normal XHR path and has no signed recipient token or confirmation step. Topic URLs are predictable for public topics, so a third-party site can force an authenticated visitor to navigate to one and mute/downgrade that visitor's topic notifications; browser prefetchers or link scanners can also trigger the change. The GET should only render a confirmation, with the mutation performed by a CSRF-protected POST, or the email link should use a recipient-bound signed token with appropriate one-click semantics.

findings.title: The endpoint crashes for users without an existing TopicUser row
findings.body: `find_by` can return nil for a logged-in user who has never visited or otherwise interacted with the topic, which is normal for a public topic reachable through this route. The following `tu.notification_level` dereference then raises a NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of applying the requested preference. Use a get-or-create path (such as `TopicUser.change`) and treat the absent row as the default notification level.

findings.title: Directly saving TopicUser bypasses notification preference invariants
findings.body: This save bypasses `TopicUser.change`, the standard path that sets `notifications_changed_at`, records `notifications_reason_id` as `user_changed`, and publishes the level change. In particular, topic-user records created only while sending an email have a nil notification reason; after this action leaves that reason nil, the auto-track logic in `TopicUser.update_last_read` is allowed to promote a muted user back to tracking when they later read the topic. Other open clients also do not receive the MessageBus update. Compute the desired level and persist it through `TopicUser.change` so the unsubscribe is recorded as an explicit user choice.

findings.title: The added test does not verify that the per-topic unsubscribe URL is rendered
findings.body: The test now supplies `unsubscribe_url`, but its only body assertion checks for the unchanged user-preferences URL. It never asserts that `/t/1234/unsubscribe` appears in the text or HTML email, so the suite would still pass if the new interpolation were omitted or the per-topic link were broken. Add assertions for the rendered topic-specific link, plus a request-level test for the notification-level transition.
